Though this appeal is coming up for admission, with the consent of the learned counsel appearing for the parties, the same is taken up for final disposal.

2. Appellant-claimants have preferred this appeal against the Judgment and Award dated 11th February, 2019 passed in MVC No.322 of 2017 by the Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-X, Hungund (for short hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal").
3.
For the sake of convenience, the parties in this appeal are referred to with their rank and status before the Tribunal.

4. Brief relevant facts that to led to filing this appeal are that, claimants filed petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation as to death of one NC:
2024:KHC-D:9831-DB Mariyappa Mallappa Doddamani.

It is stated in the claim petition that on 28th February, 2014 at about 10.30 pm, when said Mariyappa was proceeding on motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-29/C-5373 from Hungund towards Kushtagi on Hungund-Hospet National Highway, one lorry bearing Registration No.KA-28/B-9147 was parked near Hanumnal cross of Hungund Taluk on the highway without any indication and when the rider of motorcycle reached there, because of the reflection of lights of oncoming vehicles, the lorry could not be seen and he dashed against the parked lorry, as a result, he sustained grievous injuries all over the body and died on the spot.
It is further stated that prior to accident, deceased was hale and healthy and was aged 50 years.
He was earning Rs.20,000/- per month from doing labour work and was also getting Rs.2.00 lakh per annum from agriculture.
Because of the unfortunate death, the family has lost the love and affection of the only breadwinner in the family and also put to financial hardship.

It is also contended that the respondents 1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending lorry,
are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
On all these grounds sought to allow the appeal.

In response to notice, respondents 1 and 2 appeared through their counsel and filed statement of objection.

In his statement of objection, respondent No.1 has stated that the lorry was insured with the respondent No.2- Insurance Company and the policy was in force and if the court comes to conclusion that the claimants are entitled for compensation, the respondent No.2-Insurance Company may be directed to pay the compensation and hence sought to dismiss the claim petition as against respondent No.1.
6.
Respondent No.2 has denied the petition averments as false.
It is contended that the alleged accident was due to gross negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
It is further contended that the driver of the offending lorry was not having effective driving licence to drive the said class of vehicle as on the date of accident.
It is admitted that the vehicle was insured and the same is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is further contended that the owner and insurer of the motorcycle are necessary parties to the proceedings.
It is also denied about the age and occupation of the deceased.

Further, the compensation claimed is highly NC:
2024:KHC-D:9831-DB exorbitant and excessive and on all these grounds, sought to dismiss the claim petition.
7.
Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal formulated appropriate issues.

To substantiate their case,
claimant No.1 got examined as PW1 and got marked seven documents as Exhibits P1 to P7.
The Driving licence of the deceased was marked with the consent of the learned counsel for the respondent.

On closure of claimants' side evidence, respondent No.2 examined one person as RW1 and marked one document as Exhibit R1.
8.

Upon hearing the arguments of the parties, the Tribunal allowed claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.5,13,626/- with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Tribunal has saddled 50% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.

Being aggrieved by the judgment and award of the Tribunal, the appellant-claimants have preferred this appeal questioning the negligence on the part of the deceased to the extent of 50%
and also seeking enhancement of compensation.

Sri Shivakumar S. Badawadagi, learned counsel appearing for the appellant/claimants submit that the impugned judgment and award is liable to be modified by awarding compensation as claimed in the claim petition.

He submits that there is no evidence on record to show that there is negligence on the part of the deceased and the Tribunal has erred in holding that the deceased has contributed 50% for occurrence of the accident and the respondents have not led any evidence to prove their defence.
Hence, adverse inference ought to have been drawn against the respondents.

He further submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in considering the income of the deceased only at Rs.8,000/- per month though it is claimed in the claim petition that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month by doing agriculture work.
Hence, the same is on the lower side.

Further, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on other heads is not in accordance with Renavva W/O Mariyappa Madar @ Doddamani vs Chandrashekar S/O Sangabgouda Goudar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16714710/

1. Whether the Tribunal is justified in assessing the negligence of the deceased to an extent of 50%?
2. Whether the appellant/claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?
3. What order of award?

sentences.text: A holistic view of the evidence has to be taken into consideration by the Tribunal and strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner need not be established by the claimants.
The claimants have to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt cannot be applied while considering the petition seeking compensation on account of death or injury in a road traffic accident.
To the same effect is the observation made by this Court in Dulcina Fernandes vs. Joaquim Xavier Cruz (2013) 10 SCC 646 which has referred to the aforesaid judgment in Bimla Devi.

This is because the Appellant herein is seeking - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:9831-DB compensation for the death of his son in the accident which occurred on account of the negligence on the part of the driver of the tanker lorry, causing the accident on the said date.

The impact of the accident was that the rider of the motorcycle sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.
To substantiate this, one witness was examined as PW1.
She has deposed as to the accident as is alleged in the claim petition and also produced documents.

sentences.text: Thereafter, police have rushed to spot and conducted spot panchanama and inquest panchanama in the presence of panchas and prepared rough sketch, obtained post-mortem report and motor vehicle inspection report and recorded the statement of witnesses and after thorough investigation, the Investigation Officer submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the lorry for commission of offence punishable under Section 287 Indian Penal Code and Section 187 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
After filing the charge sheet, the case was registered in CC No.482 of 2014 on the file of Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Hungund and summons was issued to the accused.

In response to summons, accused appeared before the Court and pleaded guilty for commission of offence under Sections 287 of Indian Penal Code and Section 187 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and was sentenced to pay fine of Rs.600/- for offence punishable under Section 287 of Indian Penal Code and Rs.300/- for the offence punishable under Section 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and total fine amount of Rs.900/- was also paid by the accused.
It is the driver of the offending - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:9831-DB lorry who had parked the vehicle negligently without following the Road Regulations and Rules.
The Insurance Company has contended that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the deceased.
To substantiate the same, the respondents have not adduced any legal evidence before the Tribunal.
RW1 has stated that the deceased has contributed to the alleged accident.
This evidence is not substantiated by any eye-witness.
Admittedly, RW1 is not the eye-witness to the accident.

Hence, without any supporting evidence on record the merely the oral evidence of RW1 is not sufficient to come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.

It is admitted fact that the Investigation Officer has submitted charge sheet against the deceased rider of motorcycle for commission of offence punishable under Sections 279, 304-A of the Indian Penal Code or any other offences

On careful scrutiny of the entire evidence on record, absolutely there is no evidence to show that the accident occurred due to contributory negligence on the part of the deceased rider of the motorcycle.

Further, a perusal of rough sketch and mahazar clearly indicates that the driver of the lorry parked the same on the tar road without any indicator and caused obstruction to the ongoing Renavva W/O Mariyappa Madar @ Doddamani vs Chandrashekar S/O Sangabgouda Goudar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16714710/

sentences.text: Accordingly, the Tribunal has committed an error in holding that the accident occurred due to contributory negligence of the rider of the motorcycle to an extent of 50% without any evidence.

On re-consideration, re-examination and re-appreciation of the entire evidence on record,
and also keeping in mind the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MATHEW ALEXANDER (supra), we are of the considered opinion that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the driver of the offending lorry.
Accordingly, we answer point No.1 in the negative.

With regard to the quantum of compensation is concerned, the claimants have not produced any legal/acceptable evidence to determine the income of the deceased.
However, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month considering the age and occupation of the deceased, which need not be faulted with.
The Tribunal has considered the age of the deceased as 50 years on the basis of post-mortem report Exhibit P5.
The petitioner No.1 has produced Exhibit P8 smart card of driving licence with the consent of the respondent No.2, which reveals the date of birth of the deceased as 01st July, 1971.
The accident occurred on 28th February, 2014.
Hence, the age of the deceased would be 42 year, 7 month and 27 days as on the date of the accident.

In view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of SARLA VERMA v. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION LTD. AND ANOTHER reported in (2009)6 SCC 121, the appropriate multiplier applicable for the person in the age group 41-45 would be 14 and not 13 as adopted by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: If the same is added, the monthly income of the deceased would be Rs.10,000/-.
As there are three dependents, one-third has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
Accordingly, the loss of dependency would be Rs.11,20,000/- (Rs.10,000/- x 12 x 14 x 2/3).

Further, the Tribunal has not awarded compensation as per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of PRANAY SETHI (supra)
towards loss of consortium and other heads.
